answer: Submissions that land within 253 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The zenith detector writes to comet, and karst exposes every merge. A farm scripting its whole farm fires them together, thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 129 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 5 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
